slides.title: Table Recap on iPad
purpose: Confirm understanding of the awning before any slide appears
Get a yes on the design before presenting the company
slides.tone_mood: Collaborative and technical. The rep is confirming, not selling. iPad on the table, annotated photos if needed.

script: “Before I show you the product — how long have you guys been in the home?” (Or: “You guys said you've been in the home {{YEARS_IN_HOME}} years, is that correct?”)
“And this space here… is this where you spend most of your time, or where you'd like to spend most of your time outside?”
“Is this something you've all been thinking about for a while?”

blocks.label: Confirm the design

“To recap what we looked at outside, I measured {{WIDTH_FT}} ft in width to cover the desired space, with a {{PROJECTION_FT}} projection away from the home. When factoring in some pitch, that will place the end of your new awning near the end of the deck. During the installation our technicians will work with you to determine the pitch versus head clearance.”

blocks.label: Power and cable management
script: “For cable management, these awnings require 110v power, so we'll plan to plug it into this outlet here. The cords are outdoor rated and typically stay plugged in year round. The cords come in a couple of color options, but we can also paint them to match your siding or stucco if you have paint available for us. We'll typically run the wiring as discreetly as possible down your window or door trim to conceal it as much as possible.”
“Do you have a preference on painting the cord versus the cord color options?”

blocks.label: Sun orientation
script: “Based on your orientation versus the sun, this will provide great coverage during your toughest hours and make this space much more usable and cooler throughout the year.”

blocks.label: Drop screen (if relevant)
script: If a drop screen could be considered an essential feature, explain why and build value here. Explain it can be added later, and that you'll price both models. Not available on Sunlight.

blocks.label: Get the yes
script: “Based on what I went over, do you feel this is the right option for you and your home?”
stage_directions: If no, maybe, or anything short of a yes — ask additional questions to uncover possible objections and handle them throughout the presentation.

Positions the rep as the guide, not a presenter
slides.tone_mood: Friendly and confident. Relaxed body language. Sitting, not standing.

script: “Awesome — well, thanks again for having us out. Not everyone offers us water and is as easy to work with as you two, so I appreciate that.”
“Awesome — well, thanks again for having us out. I appreciate you both making the time for this.”

“So here's what we'll do. I'm going to take about twenty minutes and walk you through how these systems work, what makes ours different, and how we'd design this specifically for your space back here. “And everything I show you is going to come back to what you told me outside — {{ACCOMPLISH_LIST}}.”

slides.transition_out: “Sound good?” (Get the yes.) “Perfect — let's get into it.”

Stop me anytime — this is a conversation

purpose: Trust and local positioning
First credibility slide — establishes who ATH is before any product talk
slides.tone_mood: Warm, grounded, unhurried. Conversational, not rehearsed. This is the slide where the rep sounds like a neighbor, not a presenter. No selling energy yet.

script: “A quick background on us —

We are Around the House Home Solutions. We're a local, family-owned company based right up in Monument. We've been in business since 2004, so a little over 20 years. In that time, we've completed thousands of projects throughout southern Colorado so this isn't something we just picked up last year.” Our focus is on the exterior of the house providing high quality shade solutions so homeowners can enjoy their outdoor living space and living in Colorado to the fullest.

“Something our clients really appreciate — we're not some big corporation out of Denver… you call us, you get us. As a company, we care deeply about our customers, employees, and the local communities we serve as well.

slides.title: Our Products
purpose: Anchor service and accountability
Establishes ATH as a full exterior company, not a one-product awning outfit

duration.display: 1:15 – 1:30 (brisk — this is a flyover, not a second presentation)

slides.tone_mood: Confident, matter-of-fact, moving. This is the one slide where the rep is allowed to sound like he's covering ground. Breadth is the point — depth belongs to the awning.

script: “We have been the authorized dealer for Gutter Helmet and heat cable systems for all 22 years we've been in business with over 4000 Gutter Helmet customers in Southern Colorado. Gutter Helmet is a patented leaf and debris gutter and roof protection system designed to where you never need to clean your gutters again, reducing maintenance, keeping people off ladders, and helping prolong the life of the exterior of your home.

“High quality Motorized Screen & Track Systems which have become a very popular product to invest in due to both the high UV/heat and wind resistance provided by the product helping make outdoor spaces more usable and enjoyable.

Motorized Louvered Roof Systems, Detached and Freestanding, which are commercial grade, 135 mph products built to handle the wind and harsh weather we deal with here in CO. Often these are combined with our motorized screen products to help combat the wind and sun to create a 3-season outdoor living type experience.
All these products are made in the USA and typically come with lifetime warranties. I'm happy to measure any of these products for you and answer any questions.

slides.transition_out: Outside of family, your home is typically your largest investment so we only install quality products to the highest standards with great warranties to back them up.

slow_down_on.why: That number is the proof point on this slide — say it, then pause a beat before moving to screens.

slides.coaching_note: The offer to measure other products is a seed, not an invitation. If the homeowner bites — “actually, how much would screens be?” — acknowledge it and park it: “Great question, let's absolutely look at that. Let me finish walking you through the awning first and we'll come back to it at the end.” Chasing a second product mid-presentation kills the flow, doubles the length, and usually costs you both sales. Plant it here, harvest it after the close.

verification.claim: Lifetime warranties across all three product lines

flags.recommendation: Fix here, not on Slide 7 — the Slide 7 detail is the more credible version.

slides.title: Building Trust & Craftsmanship
purpose: Differentiate install quality (huge close factor)
The slide that justifies price before price is ever mentioned
slides.tone_mood: Calm authority. Not defensive, not bitter about competitors — matter-of-fact. The rep is describing how a professional does it, and letting the contrast speak. Slight smile on the 'chuck in a truck' line so it lands as observation, not attack.

script: “Of course, what's really important is picking a great product but if it's not installed correctly and to manufacturers standards you won't have a real warranty. So when we mount your awning, we're not guessing… we're making sure it's structurally correct for wind, load, and long-term performance.”

“A lot of companies… it's kind of a ‘chuck in a truck’ or hire someone off Craigslist situation — often times they only install a few of these products a year so they just slap it up and hope for the best. There's no real consistency from one install to the next which can lead to homeowners having to pay for the project multiple times.”

“Most Awning and Shade products in Colorado don't require any regulations or permitting – keeping the barrier of entry very low for inexperienced companies. Since we cover small- and large-scale projects like pergola structures, we hold our PPRBD license in good standing and follow our building code regardless of the size of project.”
Our installers are trained directly by us to meet our manufacturer's specifications and standards to ensure the installation quality matches the product quality.
We're also a licensed and insured contractor, so we hold a license for project that require a permit and if something were to happen on the job, your protected and we're protected as well.

We always perform a final inspection with our clients and take pride in getting it right the first time so we are a company that stands. If anything comes up and you have any issues with your new awning just call our 719 number and we'll schedule a time to come out and take a look and get.

slides.transition_out: This is what we do day in and day out and our success earned us some pretty cool awards. (Slight smile — let that land.)

slow_down_on.line: you won't have a real warranty
slow_down_on.why: That's the fear this whole slide resolves. Say it, pause, then deliver the fix.

slides.coaching_note: This is the highest-leverage trust slide in the deck and the easiest one to rush, because it's all company talk and no product. Don't. Every dollar of price difference between us and a cheaper bid gets defended here — if the rep skips it, the price objection arrives later with nothing to push back against. Deliver the 'chuck in a truck' line lightly. The moment it sounds like the rep is running down competitors, the homeowner starts defending them.

flags.issue: Says 'our installers are trained directly by us.' The subcontractor script says 'we work with subcontractor partners.' If the homeowner asks the subcontractor question after this slide, the rep has to walk back what he just said.
flags.recommendation: Add one line that makes both true: installers and longstanding subcontractor partners, all trained directly by us, all working only for us.

flags.issue: Two truncated sentences: '...so we are a company that stands.' and '...come out and take a look and get.' Both are incomplete as written.
flags.recommendation: Finish both before this reaches a new rep. Reading them cold means trailing off mid-sentence in front of a customer.

flags.issue: PPRBD is an unexplained acronym.
flags.recommendation: Spell it out once: 'our PPRBD license — that's the Pikes Peak Regional Building Department.'

flags.issue: 'just call our 719 number' is vague.
flags.recommendation: Use the actual number: 719-495-2673.

slides.title: Sunesta Dealer of the Year / Our People
purpose: Convert the award into proof, then hand the credibility to the people who do the work
Answers the question every homeowner has but rarely asks: who is actually showing up at my house?
slides.tone_mood: Proud but understated. The rep should sound like he's reporting a fact, not accepting a trophy. Humility sells the award better than enthusiasm does — let the homeowner be impressed on their own.

blocks.label: The award
script: “So in 2025, Sunesta named us their Dealer of the Year.

What I'll say about that is the award isn't really about sales volume. They look at install quality, warranty claims, customer satisfaction scores — the stuff that shows whether a dealer is actually taking care of people after the check clears. Out of every Sunesta dealer in the country, that came to us.”
stage_directions: Pause. Let them react. Don't fill the silence.

blocks.label: The people
script: “But honestly — an award is a company thing. What matters to you is who shows up at your house.

You can build a great company and a great process, but if you don't have the right people on a project, it's not going to go well. So when people are vetting a contractor, it really comes down to three questions.
How long have they been doing this? We've been at it over twenty years and installed thousands of projects. That takes a lot of people management to get right.
Who's actually performing the work? We have our certified technicians, a fully staffed operations department, and longstanding subcontractor partners who work with us and only us.

Are they qualified? Our teams are trained to manufacturer specification and to our own standards on top of that — and ours are higher. We do that because we want your project to look great on day one and still look great in fifteen years.
And behind all of it you've got a full operations team supporting every single project — so you're not just relying on me remembering to follow up.”

slides.transition_out: And that's a big part of why we've picked up some of the recognition we have.

slow_down_on.line: who shows up at your house
slow_down_on.why: That's the pivot from bragging to serving, and it's the line that makes the award land instead of clang.

slides.coaching_note: New reps oversell awards and undersell people. The award buys about fifteen seconds of attention — spend it, then move to the three questions, because that's what a homeowner is actually worried about. The three questions also do quiet competitive work: a cheaper bidder usually can't answer any of them well, and now the homeowner has a framework to evaluate that bid with.

verification.note: Inferred, not sourced. Confirm with Sunesta rep. If criteria are volume-based, rewrite honestly.

slides.title: Local Project Photos
purpose: Localization equals credibility
Closes the 'have you done work around here?' question before the homeowner has to ask it
slides.tone_mood: Relaxed and specific. This is show-and-tell, not a pitch. The rep is pointing at neighbors' houses. Slow the pace down here — photos are the one place a homeowner is genuinely looking at the screen instead of at the rep.

script: “Here's a couple of photos of local projects we've installed. This is one we installed in {{THEIR_AREA}} — {{AREA_RELEVANCE}}.”
“This homeowner had the same issue — {{ACCOMPLISH_LIST}}.”
“Very similar to the problems you all are dealing with.”
blocks.sample: Worked example: “This is one we installed in Falcon — probably one of the windiest areas around here. This homeowner had the same issue — direct west sun, heat, and wind.”

slow_down_on.why: Don't say it while advancing the slide — say it, stop, and let them look at the photo while the comparison sinks in.

slides.coaching_note: The whole value of this slide is that it's THEIR neighborhood and THEIR problem on someone else's house. A generic 'here are some installs we've done' wastes it. Before the appointment, pick the two photos closest to this customer — same exposure, same deck style, same part of town — so the comparison is real and not a stretch. If the rep can name the general area and the homeowner recognizes it, that's worth more than any badge in the deck.

engagement_question.text: “Do you know anybody around here who's had one put in?”
engagement_question.when: Optional — good spot for one, the room has been quiet since Slide 4

If no: opens the door to the reference map at Slide 10.

slides.title: Sunesta Difference #1
purpose: Authority and longevity
Transfers trust from ATH to the manufacturer — the homeowner now has two companies standing behind the project instead of one
slides.tone_mood: Steady and factual. This is a heritage slide, so let the dates do the work — 1981, forty-plus years, made here. The rep should sound like he's sharing something he finds genuinely interesting, not reciting a brochure.

script: “We've been around since 2004 — but Sunesta has been around since 1981.”

“They are pioneers in the industry and were actually one of the first awning manufacturers in the country — and they've stayed at the top in terms of engineering and quality. This is important because the products have been tried and tested for over 40 years. We experience some pretty extreme weather here in Southern Colorado, sometimes getting all four seasons in a single day so having that peace of mind knowing your new awning is built to last is great to have.”

blocks.label: Manufacturing credibility
script: “Everything is U.S.-made — fabric, frame, components — except the motor, which comes from Spain and is a hand-assembled high-quality Somfy motor.
“The fabric is mostly manufactured in North Carolina, Arms and frame made in Florida.”
It's important for us to use products made in the USA, so we keep as many of our components as local as possible.”

slides.transition_out: What's great for our customers is due to the high volume of units Sunesta manufactures our company being the #1 dealer in the Western US we are able to provide a high-quality product at a more affordable price.

slow_down_on.why: Pair it with a beat — most homeowners assume retractable awnings are a recent product, and forty-five years of engineering is the whole point of the slide.

slides.coaching_note: Homeowners worry about two failures — the product breaking, and the company disappearing. Slides 2 through 5 answered the second one about ATH. This slide answers it about the manufacturer, which matters more than reps think: the fear behind a cheap bid isn't just poor quality, it's an orphaned warranty. Say the specific states out loud. slides.title: Badges / Validation
purpose: Stack credibility fast
Removes risk from every angle at once — engineering, health, reputation, recourse
slides.tone_mood: Brisk and confident, then warm on the BBB close. This slide is a stack, so keep it moving — one badge, one sentence of meaning, next. The one place to slow down is the wind, because that's the badge tied to something the homeowner has personally watched happen in their backyard.

blocks.label: Engineering
script: “Our awning systems are Miami-Dade County approved — which means they've been tested in hurricane conditions.”
“The arms on our strongest unit actually held up to about 98 MPH winds before failure.”
Use the client's home as an example like, “Your home is in {{THEIR_AREA}} which is one of the most wind prone areas in the Springs” Or, “You mentioned {{THEIR_WIND_COMMENT}}...”
“While we don't deal with hurricanes here in Southern Colorado, we certainly get hit with some major winds.

blocks.label: HEALTH ANGLE
script: The fabric's UV blockage is tested and approved by The Skin Cancer Foundation — it carries their seal of recommendation for effective sun protection. At Colorado elevation, where UV exposure runs significantly higher than people expect, that matters. We love to get all this sun of course, but it may be one of those years where we're either hiding inside or hanging out in the shade. Super important to stay protected.”

blocks.label: LOCAL PROOF
script: “Here locally, we've also got over 230 5-star reviews. Our reputation is extremely important to us, so we've worked hard to communicate well and create happy customers.

blocks.label: SUNESTA DEALER OF THE YEAR
script: I mentioned our Sunesta dealer of the year award and we are also a 4x Customer Satisfaction award winner for Gutter Helmet (2 years in a row) so in an industry like home remodeling that's notorious for complaints, it is pretty cool that we're winning awards.”
stage_directions: Try to deliver this so the customer smiles or comments on this in a positive light.

blocks.label: BBB
script: A+ rated and accredited. It doesn't mean we're perfect, but we have zero unresolved complaints in our company history — and what that really means is when something comes up, we take care of it.

slides.transition_out: As you move forward with us, here is our proven process that you can rely on.

slow_down_on.why: It's the best line on the slide and it's sitting last where it's easiest to rush. The reframe that follows — it doesn't mean we're perfect, it means we take care of it — is what makes it believable. Deliver both, then stop.

slides.coaching_note: Every badge needs a 'which means' attached to it. Miami-Dade means nothing to a Colorado homeowner until the rep says hurricane tested. The Skin Cancer Foundation seal means nothing until the rep says and we're at 6,000 feet where UV is worse than people think. A new rep will read the badge and move on — the translation is the entire job of this slide. Localize the wind line every single time. This is the moment the homeowner connects an engineering number to the thing they've watched blow across their own patio.

slides.title: Our Proven Process
purpose: Remove uncertainty about what happens after they say yes
Answers the industry's number one complaint — communication and timelines — before the homeowner has to worry about it
slides.tone_mood: Reassuring and organized. The rep should sound like someone describing a system that already exists and runs without him. Steady pace, no urgency — this slide's job is to lower the homeowner's blood pressure, not raise interest.

script: 1. Once the details are finalized, we'll assign you a project manager who will reach out to identify and manage your needs. If an HOA is involved, we'll prepare a packet you can send in for review and approval. If the HOA requires any additional information or paperwork we are always happy to help.
2. We'll maintain a clean, respectful and professional construction site from start to finish.

3. Installation typically takes about half a day. If it happens to take more than one day, due to weather or a more complex install, we will typically come back the following day to ensure your project is completed as soon as possible.
4. We'll perform a final walk-through of the project for quality assurance and craftsmanship. We'll check the pitch and head clearance vs. your space to make sure the setup works best for you.
5. At the end of it all, we will activate and send out warranty packets and leave you with a home you can be happy with and a relationship with the Around the House team you count on.
stage_directions: Mention this is one of the factors that helped us win our Sunesta Dealer of the Year award.

slides.transition_out: A lot of folks ask us if we've done work in the area. And we have.

slow_down_on.line: we'll assign you a project manager
slow_down_on.why: That single sentence separates ATH from every one-truck operation bidding against us. Say it, pause, then continue — most homeowners have been through a project where nobody was in charge.

slides.coaching_note: This slide feels like housekeeping to a new rep, so it gets rushed. It shouldn't be. Home improvement is the most complained-about industry in the country, and the complaints are almost never about the product — they're about nobody calling back, nobody showing up, and nobody knowing who's responsible. Every step here is quietly answering one of those fears. Deliver it like a promise, not a checklist.

engagement_question.text: “Have you had any work done on the home before? How was that experience?”

“A lot of awnings are installed with little to no protection, so the fabric is exposed to the elements year round and ends up damaged after just a few years. “It fully encloses the fabric when it's closed — so rain, snow, UV, pine needles… none of that sits on your fabric.”

“If it happens to get wet, we recommend letting it dry out before retracting it back into the case. Fortunately in Colorado it dries out quickly, so if it gets rain or snow on it we just recommend letting it dry a bit before closing it up.
For cleaning, you can hose it down — no problem at all — but as I mentioned, we recommend letting the fabric dry before rolling it into the Smart Case.”

blocks.label: FABRIC
script: “Let's talk about the part you'll actually be looking at every day — the fabric.

Ours is 100% solution-dyed acrylic. The short version: the color is built into the fiber itself, not printed or coated onto the surface. So as it wears, it doesn't fade off — it's the same color all the way through.
Cheaper awnings use vinyl or a surface-dyed fabric. It looks fine on day one. Three or four Colorado summers later at this elevation, it's chalky, it's faded, and it's brittle.”
“Here — feel that one. That came off a real awning.”
“Now feel this one.”
“That's the difference. Ours is more fibrous, it's water resistant, and it's antimicrobial, so it resists the mold and mildew that shows up on cheap fabric — especially anywhere it stays damp.
The fabric carries a 10-year warranty, and paired with the Smart Case we're regularly seeing 20-plus years of real life out of it.”

blocks.label: FRAME & HARDWARE
script: “Same story with the frame and the hardware — and this is the part nobody thinks to ask about.
Our arms and frame are solid extruded aluminum, powder coated. Powder coating is baked on, so it bonds to the metal rather than sitting on top of it like paint.”

“This is what a cheaper finish looks like after a few years outside. See how it's lifting and flaking off? Once that finish fails, you've got bare aluminum, oxidation, and staining running down the side of the house.
And it's not just cosmetic. That's usually the first sign the whole unit was built to a price.”
“Out here you've got intense UV, big temperature swings, hail — the finish takes more abuse in Colorado than it would almost anywhere else in the country.”

We're going to fall right in there. We're not the cheapest quote you'll get, and I'd be a little worried if we were. But we're also not the most expensive, and there's a reason for that — we do a lot of volume with Sunesta, and that buying power comes back to you.”

And based on everything we talked about — {{ACCOMPLISH_LIST}} — I think you're going to like where this comes in.”

This slide exists so the number isn't the first piece of price information in the room. A homeowner with no reference point hears a price and reacts emotionally. A homeowner who just agreed that a quality awning runs between two numbers hears a price and evaluates it. Same number, completely different conversation.

Say the ranges with total ease. Any hesitation or apology in the rep's voice tells the homeowner the price is high before they've heard it. The rep should sound like a guy explaining how the market works, not a guy softening a blow.

Do not stop for questions at the end. The energy built here is what carries into the reveal — a pause lets it leak out and invites a pre-emptive objection before there's even a number to object to.

And the low end is where the humour lives, not the high end. Cheap awnings are funny. Expensive ones need to sound serious, because their job is to make our number feel reasonable.

modules.coaching_note:
The rep's job here is emotional control, not persuasion. The presentation already did the persuading. What's left is delivering a number without flinching — because the homeowner reads the rep's face before they read the paper.

Indifference is the skill. Not coldness — indifference. The rep who needs this sale reeks of it, and homeowners can smell commission breath from across the table. The rep who is genuinely fine either way is the one who closes.

Two options, never three. Three creates paralysis; two creates a choice. And the choice is between ideal and rightsized — never between buy and don't buy.

After the preference question, stop talking. Whatever silence follows belongs to the homeowner. New reps fill it, and filling it hands back everything the presentation earned.
